mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{For the heat equation } \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}, \text{ which of these solutions represents a transient (time-dependent) solution?}\)
\(\text{For a heat conduction problem with both ends insulated, the boundary conditions are:}\)
\(\text{In Example 4 of the heat equation section, the initial temperature is triangular with maximum k at the center. The Fourier coefficients } B_n \text{ are non-zero for:}\)
\(\text{For a rod with initial temperature } u(x,0)=kx(l-x) \text{ and ends kept at 0°C, the Fourier coefficient } B_n \text{ is:}\)
\(\text{When solving the heat equation with non-zero boundary conditions, the transient solution } u_2(x,t) \text{ satisfies:}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Solve heat equation with } u(0,t)=0, u(l,t)=0, u(x,0)=x(l-x).\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{At } t=0: x(l-x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{l} \int_0^l x(l-x) \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Evaluate: } B_n = \frac{4l^2}{n^3\pi^3}[1-(-1)^n]. \text{ For odd } n, B_n = \frac{8l^2}{n^3\pi^3}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } u(x,t) = \frac{8l^2}{\pi^3} \sum_{n=\text{odd}} \frac{1}{n^3} \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A bar of length } l \text{ has ends kept at } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=x(l-x). \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Boundary conditions: } \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}(0,t)=0, \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}(l,t)=0.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=A_0 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty A_n \cos\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{At } t=0: f(x) = A_0 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty A_n \cos\frac{n\pi x}{l}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Fourier cosine coefficients: } A_0 = \frac{1}{l} \int_0^l f(x) dx, A_n = \frac{2}{l} \int_0^l f(x) \cos\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Hence the solution is obtained by substituting these coefficients.}\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A bar of length } l \text{ has insulated ends. Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=f(x). \text{ Find the temperature distribution.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Heat equation: \(u_t = \alpha^2 u_{xx}.\) BCs: \(u(0,t)=0\), \(u(l,t)=0.\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(u(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Initial condition: \(u(x,0)= \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{By orthogonality, \(B_1=1\), \(B_n=0\) for \(n\neq1.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(u(x,t)= \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 \pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Interpretation: single mode decaying exponentially with time constant \(\tau = l^2/(\alpha^2\pi^2).\)}\) (3 Marks)
Sketch temperature profiles at different times: amplitude decreases but shape remains sinusoidal. (2 Marks)
\(\text{As \(t\to\infty\), \(u\to 0\) (steady state zero temperature).}\) (2 Marks)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A rod of length  $l$ with insulated sides has its ends kept at zero temperature.}\\ \text{The initial temperature is $u(x,0)= \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right).$  Find the temperature distribution  $u(x,t).$}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Heat equation: \(u_t = \alpha^2 u_{xx}\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{General solution: \(u(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(u(x,0)= x(\pi-x) = \sum B_n \sin(nx).\)}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Compute \(B_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi} \int_0^{\pi} x(\pi-x) \sin(nx) dx.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Integration: use formula or integrate by parts. Result: \(B_n = \dfrac{4}{\pi n^3}[1-(-1)^n].\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(B_n = \dfrac{8}{\pi n^3}\) for \(n\) odd, \(0\) for \(n\) even.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{So \(u(x,t)= \sum\limits_{n \text{ odd}} \dfrac{8}{\pi n^3} \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Write first few terms: \(u(x,t)= \dfrac{8}{\pi}\left[ \sin(x) e^{-\alpha^2 t} + \dfrac{1}{27} \sin(3x) e^{-9\alpha^2 t} + \cdots \right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
